They weigh exactly the same — one kilogram. This is a classic trick question designed to catch people who reflexively answer "steel" because it's denser or "feathers" because thebuoyancy myth confuses them. The material doesn't matter; only the total mass does.

A kilogram is a unit of mass, not weight, so even in different gravitational fields, a kilogram of anything has identical mass (and, on Earth at the same location, identical weight). The feathers would simply take up far more space — you'd need a huge pile of them, while the steel could be a small block or cube
